title: Sequence Quality Control
author: James E Thornton Jr
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j2icqce

steps.title: Prepare HPC Environment and Data
steps.instruction: Log into the HPC and prepare the FASTQ files for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Login to the HPC using: ssh hpc $ ocelote
Navigate to the directory containing FASTQ files: cd /rsgrps/bh_class/username/fastq (replace username with your own)
Uncompress FASTQ files if they have a .gz extension using: gunzip *.gz

steps.title: Generate Sequence Quality Reports
steps.instruction: Use FastQC to visualize the quality of the sequence reads.

substeps.instruction: Load the FastQC tool: module load fastqc
Create an output directory: mkdir /rsgrps/bh_class/username/quality_control (replace username with your own)
Run FastQC on all fastq files and output to the created directory: fastqc *.fastq -o /rsgrps/bh_class/username/quality_control

steps.title: Transfer and View Quality Reports
steps.instruction: Move the HTML reports to a local machine for viewing.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to the quality_control directory: cd /rsgrps/bh_class/username/quality_control
Delete the .zip folders to keep only .html files: rm -rf ./*.zip
Transfer HTML files to local machine via SCP: scp [NETID]@login.hpc.arizona.edu:/rsgrps/bh_class/jetjr/quality_control/*.html . (replace [NETID] and path with your own)
Alternatively, if SCP fails, push files to GitHub: mkdir ~/abe487/fastqc, cp *.html ~/abe487/fastqc, cd ~/abe487/fastqc, git add *.html, git commit -m 'adding qc reports', git push
Open the .html files in a local browser (Windows/Cygwin users: navigate to C:/cygwin64/home/USER) using: open ./*.html

steps.title: Determine Quality Control Parameters
steps.instruction: Analyze the HTML summaries for each sample to determine the specific trimming and filtering parameters needed to improve read quality.

steps.title: Perform Sequence Processing with FastX
steps.instruction: Apply quality control tools from the FastX Toolkit to the sequences.

substeps.instruction: Load the FastX toolkit: module load fastx
Trim reads at specific base positions if quality drops: fastx_trimmer -f [start] -l [end] -i [Infile] -o [outfile] (Example: -f 10 -l 200)
Filter out reads failing a minimum quality score: fastq_quality_filter -q 20 -p 80 -i [infile] -o [outfile] (-q is min quality score, -p is min percent of bases meeting -q)
Remove reads below a minimum length (e.g., 70 bp): fastx_clipper -l 70 -i [infile] -o [outfile]
Collapse identical sequences into a single sequence (converts output to Fasta format): fastx_collapser -i [infile] -o [outfile]

steps.title: Optional: Automate Processing via Piping
steps.instruction: Combine multiple FastX tools into a single pipeline using a for loop and a file list.

substeps.instruction: Create a file called 'list' containing the names of the files to be processed.
Execute the piped command: % for file in `cat list`; do cat $file.fq | fastx_trimmer -f 12 -l 300 | fastq_quality_filter -q 20 -p 80 | fastx_clipper -l 60 | fastx_collapser > $file.fasta; done
